Shift standards for treat supplies for new staff
This page walks new staff through a habit of care

At the Companion Animal Travel Desk, our job is to make pet travel feel steady, kind, and easy to follow. Treat supplies are part of that care because they help us greet animals calmly, reward patience, and keep the service desk friendly for travelers and their companions. When you handle treats well, you support trust from the first hello to the final handoff.

Use only approved treats and keep them stored cleanly, sealed, and separate from paper work. Check the label before offering anything, and make sure the item suits the animal's size, species, and dietary needs. If a traveler asks about a special need, pause and bring in the passenger coordinator before you promise anything. When the traveler is calm, the pet is calm, and that makes the whole process smoother for everyone.

<<FACT F057>>

Keep your tone warm and your pace unhurried. Speak to the traveler in simple words, then turn your attention back to the animal with gentle body language. If a pet seems unsure, offer space first and treat support second. Never scatter treats near bags, doors, or shared seating, because neat handling prevents confusion and keeps the desk tidy.

For reptiles, paperwork matters just as much as the crate check. <<FACT F084>>

If anything feels unclear, do a calm stepwise review with the senior coordinator rather than guessing. Clear guidance now avoids stress later and helps the traveler leave with confidence. Remember to stay gentle, stay organized, and keep every treat choice safe, clean, and appropriate.
